title: Microlab SDK sprint: propulsion notes
content:
Context:
A very small hands-on lab ("Microlab") to get a new engineer from checkout -> sample request -> basic telemetry in ~20 minutes. This doc is a sprint scratchpad for the lab flow, fragile assumptions, and friction points we want to remove.

Goal:
- Create a 20-min live lab that proves: install, API key config, run a sample generation, collect token/cost telemetry, and exercise local error handling.
- Minimal prerequisites, low RAM footprint (works on M1 and small Linux dev VMs).
- Can be run as part of an onboarding session or async self-serve.

Audience:
- New hires (engineers & ML engineers) and developer advocates running demo workshops.

Non-goals (for this sprint):
- Full production deployment guides (that comes in next sprint).
- Exhaustive language bindings — prototype primary flow in Node + Python only.

Prerequisites (what we ask the user to have):
- Git installed, basic shell familiarity.
- Local tmux/shell optional.

High-level lab flow (target 20m):
1) Clone repo (2m)
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/sdk-examples.git microlab
2) Install minimal deps (3m)
   - Node: npm ci --prefix microlab/node/quickstart
   - Python: pip install -r microlab/python/requirements.txt --user
3) Set API key (2m)
   - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-XXXXX   # show how to create key in console (link)
4) Run sample generation (5m)
   - node microlab/node/quickstart/run.js --prompt "Summarize this paragraph"
   - python microlab/python/quickstart/run.py --prompt "Summarize this paragraph"
5) Inspect response streaming (2m)
   - show how the chunked response appears, how to abort early
6) Enable local telemetry + cost breakdown (3m)
   - run microlab/telemetry/collector locally (one file)
   - point to console metrics and show token counts in the sample event
7) Smoke tests + failure modes (3m)
   - induce network error, show retry/backoff behavior; simulate rate limit
   - copy-paste common troubleshooting commands

Detailed notes / friction points to fix:
- Large token counts: our sample prompts sometimes produce long outputs on open models. Add explicit max_tokens param in quickstart to keep latency predictable.
- API key UX: users often paste the whole bearer header instead of the key. Add a small script that detects both and normalizes.
- Windows gotchas: npm scripts assume bash. Add a lightweight Powershell alias or Windows note.
- Streaming example: current Node sample uses generic stream; add a wrapper that shows partial tokens and simple UI (progress dots).
- Telemetry integration: collectors should default to ephemeral in-memory ingestion with one CLI toggle. Avoid requiring infra (kafka, etc.) for the lab.

CLI recipes (handy commands to copy during workshop):
- Quick env check:
  - echo $SHELL; node -v; python -V
- Run node sample (short):
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-XXX node microlab/node/quickstart/run.js --prompt "What is Redwood?" --max-tokens 80
- Run python sample (short):
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-XXX python microlab/python/quickstart/run.py --prompt "What is Redwood?" --max_tokens 80
- Telemetry local run (one-liner):
  - python microlab/telemetry/run_collector.py --port 9001 &

Sample code guidance (what to show in class):
- Emphasize the request/response shape, token counts, and cost = tokens * unit_price.
- Show how to attach a request id header for the console to correlate.
- Minimal error-handling snippet: retry with exponential backoff + idempotency key for streaming resumable chunks.

Success metrics for the lab (what we measure after each run):
- Time to first successful generation (target < 6m)
- % users who complete telemetry step (target 75%)
- Average number of support tickets opened post-lab (target <= 0.1 per run)

Rollout plan for internal adoption:
- Week 0: prototype Node+Python flow, gather feedback from 3 DEX engineers. (owner: Samir)
- Week 1: iterate on telemetry collector and error-handling snippets; add Windows notes. (owner: Maya)
- Week 2: convert to a single-file "Microlab run" script for demo leads; create short slide deck (5 slides).
- Week 3: publish to DEX shared lab inventory and add to onboarding checklist. (owner: Cecilia)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want to include an auto-generated billing estimate in the quickstart, or keep it manual? (pros/cons discussed in meeting 2025-10-22).
- Should the lab include a dedicated small hosted model endpoint (to avoid noisy open model variance) or rely on local quantized model? (Tradeoffs: cost vs reproducibility)
- Need a short snippet that demonstrates routing fallback (hosted -> local) — existing APIs support this but we need a tiny sample config.

Known tickets to close before pilot:
- DEX-1287: create single-file telemetry collector with no infra deps (blocking)
- DEX-1290: add Windows-friendly npm wrappers
- DEX-1292: cap max_tokens in all quickstart examples

Appendix: quick workshop script for a 20-min session (timeboxed)
- 0:00 - 2:00 intro + goals + share repo link
- 2:00 - 5:00 clone + install (instructor runs fast path for those who fail)
- 5:00 - 9:00 set API key + run first sample
- 9:00 - 12:00 streaming + partial response demo
- 12:00 - 16:00 enable telemetry + show cost breakdown in collector UI
- 16:00 - 19:00 inject error scenario and recovery patterns
- 19:00 - 20:00 next steps + links to longer docs

Quick links (for instructor):
- Microlab repo folder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/tree/main/microlab
- Microlab confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEX/Microlab+Overview
- Slack thread: #dex-microlabs (search pinned messages)

Notes to self: keep the lab as a single-screen demo as much as possible; eliminate any manual cloud console steps besides API key creation. Consider adding a "fake server" mode to simulate spikes for failure-mode teaching.

Last updated by Cecilia (quick edits 2026-03-10): added telemetry run one-liner and updated timeline.
